title: Garmin deals UK 2026: best Forerunner, Venu and fēnix prices

description: This week's best UK Garmin deals: Forerunner 165 at £139, Forerunner 265 at £245, fēnix 8 under £500, plus good-price targets for each model.
intro:
**Short answer: the best Garmin deal for most people is the Forerunner 265 at £245.47 at Amazon (was £369.99). Beginners should get the Forerunner 165 at £139, and the fēnix 8 AMOLED has dropped to £484.99 (47mm), its lowest price yet.**

We picked 11 Garmin deals from about £120 to £500, with prices reported or checked on 25 and 26 November 2026. Almost all are at Amazon, and every card links straight to the listing.

body:
## Quick picks

- **Best overall: Garmin Forerunner 265 at £245.47.** Everything most runners need, from training readiness to recovery advice, with a sharp AMOLED screen, at 34% off.
- **Best cheap: Garmin Forerunner 165 at £139.** The same GPS and training tools in a simpler watch. If you mainly want health and gym tracking rather than running, the Vivoactive 6 at £199.74 is the better fit.
- **Best splurge: Garmin fēnix 8 AMOLED at £484.99 (47mm) or £499.99 (43mm).** Garmin's top adventure watch at its lowest price so far.

Prices come from TechRadar UK's Garmin and smartwatch deal pages, the5krunner's Amazon.co.uk price check and PriceSpy on 25 and 26 November 2026, during Amazon's Black Friday Week. Garmin prices at Amazon move several times a day, so the price on the card may be a few pounds out either way. Many of these should hold until Cyber Monday (30 November). For more watches, see our [smartwatch deals](/guides/smartwatch-deals-uk/), and for everything else on sale, [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/).

## Which Garmin should you buy?

Garmin's range looks confusing, but it splits into four families.

**Forerunner (running).** Built for runners first, with training plans, race predictions and recovery advice. The Forerunner 165 and Forerunner 70 cover beginners and parkrun regulars. The Forerunner 265 adds training readiness, training status and a more detailed look at how hard you're working, which is worth it if you train for a 10K, half or full marathon.

**Vivoactive and Venu (everyday).** These look more like a normal smartwatch and track gym sessions, walks, swims, sleep and stress well. The Vivoactive 6 is the value pick. The Venu 4 adds a speaker and microphone for calls from your phone and a more premium finish. The Venu X1 is the odd one out: a big, very thin screen with full maps, aimed at people who'd otherwise buy an Apple Watch Ultra.

**Instinct (rugged).** Chunky, tough and simple, with very long battery life. The Instinct E is the cheapest way into it; the Instinct 3 AMOLED gets a colour screen.

**fēnix (premium multisport).** Everything Garmin makes in one watch: maps, a torch, multi-band GPS, dive rating and the longest battery life of any AMOLED model here. Most people don't need one, but at under £500 it's much easier to justify than at £700 or more.

## What's a good price for a Garmin?

These are the figures we'd be happy to pay, based on this week's prices:

- Forerunner 165: under £150 (it has been £119.95 before)
- Vivoactive 6: around £200
- Forerunner 265: under £260
- Venu 4: under £350
- fēnix 8 AMOLED 47mm: under £500

If a watch is well above these, it's worth waiting. Garmin discounts heavily twice a year, at Black Friday and around Prime Day in the summer, and again for a few days in early January.

## Garmin vs Apple Watch

An Apple Watch is the better smartwatch if you have an iPhone: apps, Apple Pay, replies to messages and a sharper screen. A Garmin is the better sports watch: more accurate training data, far less charging (days or weeks, not a day and a half) and it works equally well with Android. If you run or cycle more than twice a week, we'd pick the Garmin. Our [Apple Watch deals](/guides/apple-watch-deals-uk/) guide has this week's Apple prices.

## Buying as a gift?

Garmin watches make good presents for runners because they're hard to get wrong at the Forerunner 165 or 265 level. If you're not sure about wrist size, the standard sizes (around 42–47mm) suit most adults; the 43mm fēnix and 265S are better for slim wrists. For more ideas, see our [gifts for runners](/guides/gifts-for-runners-uk/) and [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/). Plenty of runners listen to audiobooks on long runs, and Amazon's Audible offer (£0.99 a month for three months) is covered in our [Audible free trial guide](/guides/audible-free-trial-deals-uk/).

## Garmin deals FAQs

### Which Garmin watch is best for beginners?

The Forerunner 165 at £139. It has a bright screen, accurate GPS, suggested daily workouts and the same Garmin Connect app as the expensive models, without features you won't use yet.

### Is the Garmin Forerunner 265 worth it over the 165?

If you're training for a race, yes. The 265 adds training readiness, training status, HRV status and multi-band GPS. At £245.47 it's about £105 more than the 165, which is fair for a watch most runners keep for years.

### Is Garmin cheaper on Black Friday?

Yes. This week the fēnix 8, Forerunner 265, Venu X1 and Venu 4 are all at or near their lowest UK prices, and most deals are at Amazon. Prices often stay low until Cyber Monday, then creep back up in December.

### Does a Garmin work with an iPhone?

Yes. All of these watches work with iPhone and Android through the free Garmin Connect app. You get notifications on both, but you can only reply to messages from the watch on Android.

### What is the difference between the fēnix 8 43mm, 47mm and 51mm?

Only size and battery life. The features are the same; the 51mm lasts longest and the 43mm suits smaller wrists. This week the 47mm is £484.99, the 43mm £499.99 and the 51mm £549, all at Amazon.
